draft.title: Entrepreneurship and business success
card: An entrepreneur is someone who starts a business from an idea. Some traits can help turn that idea into a business that lasts.
Creativity
coming up with new ideas, or new ways to solve a problem. It helps a business offer something people want.
Persistence
keeping going when things are hard or slow. Many businesses take time to win customers.
Risk and learning
Taking a risk means trying something that might not work out. Learning from failure means asking what went wrong and fixing it next time.
draft.remember: Creativity, persistence, taking risks and learning from failure can help an idea become a lasting business.

a.q: Sam's first stall sold few cookies. He asked customers why, changed the recipe and tried again. Which trait is this?
a.why: Sam looked at what went wrong and used it to improve. That is learning from failure. Persistence is tempting, but Sam did more than keep going: he changed what he did.
a.clue: What did Sam do after the stall did poorly?

b.q: Priya's online shop made no sales for three months. She kept posting and improving her photos until orders began to arrive. Which trait did she mainly show?
b.why: Priya kept going through a slow start, which is persistence. Learning from failure is tempting because she improved her photos, but the main story is that she did not give up when sales were slow.
b.clue: What did she do while there were still no sales?

problems.detail: The first card line defines 'entrepreneur' ('someone who starts a business from an idea'), which is the idea of point 1. It is also a narrower definition than point 1's, which includes spotting an opportunity, taking the risk and bringing resources together. This point should only mention the term.

The distractor 'Persistence without change' contradicts the story, since Sam did change his recipe. It is not a trait the card names, and its qualifier makes it obviously wrong, so it gives students an easy elimination.

Priya 'kept posting and improving her photos', which also fits the card's definition of learning from failure (fixing what went wrong). Only the word 'mainly' separates persistence from learning from failure. Removing 'improving her photos' or making the improvement clearly secondary would remove the ambiguity.

proposal.title: Entrepreneurship and business success
card: Many entrepreneurs start with a good idea. Some traits can help them turn that idea into a business that lasts.
Creativity
coming up with new ideas, or new ways to solve a problem. It helps a business offer something people want.
Persistence
keeping going with the plan when things are hard or slow. Many businesses take time to win customers.
Risk and learning
Willingness to take risks means trying something that might not work, such as spending savings on stock. Learning from failure means working out what went wrong and changing it next time.
proposal.remember: Creativity, persistence, taking risks and learning from failure can help an idea become a lasting business.

a.q: Kai runs a weekend cookie stall. Which action best shows learning from failure?
opts: Asking buyers why sales fell, then fixing the problem
Opening the same stall every week through a slow year
Spending his savings on stock that might not sell
Inventing a cookie flavour nobody has tried before
a.why: Learning from failure means working out what went wrong and changing it. Asking buyers why sales fell and then fixing the problem does both. Opening the stall every week through a slow year is tempting, but it is persistence: Kai keeps going without changing anything.
a.clue: Which action responds to something that went wrong?

b.q: Priya's online shop made no sales for three months. She changed nothing, but kept posting every day until orders began to arrive. Which trait did she show?
b.why: Priya kept going with her plan through a slow start, which is persistence. Learning from failure is tempting because sales were poor, but she did not work out what went wrong or change anything.
b.clue: Did Priya change her plan, or stick with it?

a.best: Asking buyers why sales fell, then fixing the problem
